page: Amazon Web Services t2.micro is an entry-level burstable virtual machine hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It is provisioned with 1 vCPU corresponding to 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on an x86 architecture. The instance includes 1.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation of 1.0 GB per core. It contains no attached local storage, no hardware GPU accelerators, and features a baseline network bandwidth profile of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of its single-thread burstable compute allocation. The instance scored 157.0 in both stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, placing it in the bottom decile across evaluated cloud servers. PassMark testing produced an overall CPU score of 1,438.31 and a memory score of 755.64. Data transfer benchmarks measured memory bandwidth at 78.35 GB/s for small cached blocks and 10.85 GB/s for large 256 MB reads. In operational tests, the server delivered 0.51 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.12 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the t2.micro architecture is its burstable CPU model and minimal memory footprint, which make it susceptible to credit exhaustion and memory pressure under sustained or concurrent loads. However, its low resource allocation provides an economical operational tier for lightweight background processes, simple development environments, functional testing, and low-traffic web serving where high compute throughput is not required.

The server does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware, operating with a baseline network rate of 0 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks position the server within the lower decile of cloud hardware performance, generating a PassMark CPU score of 1,438.31 and 157.0 in stress-ng evaluations. Redis throughput reaches 0.51 million SET operations per second, alongside 1.12 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Because its burstable CPU allocation relies on accumulated credits and is paired with a minimal 1 GB memory envelope, the instance cannot sustain compute-intensive workflows. It is best configured for low-load microservices, prototyping, developer sandboxes, basic automation scripts, and low-traffic web hosting.
